config.title: Ionic Theming & Dark Mode

intro.title: Ionic Theming & Dark Mode
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Ionic app that allows users to toggle between light and dark themes. You will learn how to use Ionic's built-in CSS variables and Angular's data binding to dynamically change the app's appearance. The main technologies involved are Ionic's theming system, Angular components, and Capacitor for native app features. By the end, you'll understand how to implement a user-controlled dark mode switch in your mobile applications.
intro.usecase: Theming and dark mode implementation is essential for modern mobile applications where users expect personalized experiences and accessibility. In productivity apps like Notion or Todoist, dark mode reduces eye strain during nighttime use. Social media platforms like Twitter and Instagram use theming to maintain brand consistency across light and dark interfaces. E-commerce apps like Amazon implement dark mode to create comfortable browsing environments for late-night shopping. Developers need these skills to build professional applications that meet user expectations for customization and visual comfort.

objectives: Apply Ionic CSS custom properties to define color variables for light theme components.
Utilize CSS media queries to detect system dark mode preferences and apply corresponding styles.
Implement a toggle switch component to allow users to manually control dark mode activation.
Use Angular's ViewChild decorator to access and manipulate DOM elements for theme switching.
Construct a theme service to centralize dark mode state management and logic.
Execute conditional logic to apply appropriate CSS classes based on the current theme state.
Define CSS custom properties for dark theme colors and assign them to corresponding Ionic components.
Access system dark mode preferences using the matchMedia API to initialize the theme state.
Handle user interactions with the toggle switch to update the theme state and persist preferences.
Modify the root element's class list to apply global theme changes across the application.
Store user theme preferences in localStorage to maintain selections between sessions.
Retrieve stored theme preferences on application startup to restore the user's previous selection.

steps.title: Import Ionic and Angular core modules
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in these Angular and Ionic components.
steps.analogousExample:
import { Component } from '@angular/core';
import { IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar } from '@ionic/angular';
steps.seedCode: // Import Component from '@angular/core' and IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar from '@ionic/angular'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular and Ionic modules are imported for component creation.
successCriteria: The code includes import statements for Component from '@angular/core' and IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the core Angular and Ionic modules needed for building your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've imported all required symbols: Component from '@angular/core' and IonContent, IonHeader, IonTitle, IonToolbar from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statements are missing or incorrect. Make sure to import Component from '@angular/core' and the Ionic components from '@ionic/angular'.

steps.title: Create the main component
steps.instruction: Create a standalone Angular component named 'ThemeDemo' with the @Component decorator. Include an empty template and an imports array containing the Ionic modules you imported in the previous step.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define your component. The template can be empty for now.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a standalone component class ready to build upon in subsequent steps.
successCriteria: The component should be named 'ThemeDemo', use the @Component decorator, have 'standalone: true', include the Ionic imports in the imports array, and have an empty template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ThemeDemo component with the correct structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your component has: 1) the @Component decorator, 2) 'standalone: true', 3) the Ionic imports in the imports array, and 4) an empty template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't quite right. Review the example and ensure you're using the @Component decorator with the required properties.

steps.title: Add basic component structure
steps.instruction: Add the basic Ionic page structure with IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, and IonContent to your component's template.
steps.hint: Use the imported Ionic components to create a standard Ionic page layout with a header and content area.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of basic Ionic page structure in template
<ion-header>
  <ion-toolbar>
    <ion-title>My Page</ion-title>
  </ion-toolbar>
</ion-header>
<ion-content>
  <!-- Page content will go here -->
</ion-content>
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component template will have the basic Ionic page structure with header and content areas ready for adding content.
successCriteria: The template should contain IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, and IonContent components in the correct hierarchical structure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the basic Ionic page structure. This gives you a standard header with title and a content area where we'll add our theming controls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all four components: IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, and IonContent. Check that they're nested correctly - IonTitle inside IonToolbar inside IonHeader, with IonContent as a sibling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required Ionic page structure. You need to add IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, and IonContent components to create a standard Ionic page layout.

steps.title: Import Ionic utilities for theming
steps.hint: Add the import statement at the top of your file, after the existing imports.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing Ionic utilities
import { IonicModule, Platform } from '@ionic/angular';
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for IonicModule and Platform is added to the file.
successCriteria: The code includes an import statement that imports IonicModule and Platform from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported IonicModule and Platform. These utilities will help with theme detection and toggling functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the import statement isn't quite complete. Make sure you're importing both IonicModule and Platform from '@ionic/angular'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import IonicModule and Platform from '@ionic/angular'.

steps.title: Initialize theme detection state
steps.instruction: In the ThemeDemoComponent class, add a property called 'currentTheme' with type 'string' and initialize it to 'light'.
steps.hint: Add a class property inside the component class. Use TypeScript type annotation to specify it's a string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a property to track the current theme mode, initialized to 'light'.
successCriteria: The component class should contain a property named 'currentTheme' with type 'string' and initial value 'light'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the currentTheme property to track the theme mode.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the property is named exactly 'currentTheme', has type 'string', and is initialized to 'light'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required property. Add a property called 'currentTheme' with type 'string' and initial value 'light' inside the ThemeDemoComponent class.

steps.title: Add theme toggle button
steps.instruction: Add an IonButton element to your template with the text 'Toggle Theme' inside it.
steps.hint: Use the Ionic button component <ion-button> with text content between the opening and closing tags.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of adding a button to an Ionic template -->
<ion-button>Click Me</ion-button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain a button element with the text 'Toggle Theme'.
successCriteria: The code should include <ion-button>Toggle Theme</ion-button> in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a theme toggle button to your template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it uses the Ionic <ion-button> component and has the exact text 'Toggle Theme'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button wasn't added correctly. Check that you're using the Ionic button component with the correct syntax.

steps.title: Create theme toggle handler
steps.instruction: Inside the ThemeDemoComponent class, create a method called 'toggleTheme()' that switches the 'currentTheme' property between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.hint: Define a method with no parameters that checks the current value of 'currentTheme' and assigns the opposite value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can toggle the theme state between light and dark.
successCriteria: The method should be named 'toggleTheme', be defined inside the ThemeDemoComponent class, and contain logic to switch 'currentTheme' between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the toggleTheme method that switches between light and dark themes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your toggleTheme method properly switches the 'currentTheme' property between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleTheme method is missing or doesn't correctly toggle the theme. Check that you've defined the method inside the component class with the correct logic.

steps.title: Wire button to toggle handler
steps.instruction: Add an (click) event binding to the IonButton element that calls the toggleTheme() method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (click)="toggleTheme()" on the IonButton element.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of wiring a button click to a handler in Ionic Angular -->
<IonButton (click)="handleClick()">Click me</IonButton>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will be wired to the toggleTheme handler, but the handler logic isn't implemented yet.
successCriteria: The IonButton element should have an (click) attribute that calls toggleTheme().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the button click to the toggleTheme handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using Angular's event binding syntax (click)="toggleTheme()" on the IonButton.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly wired to the handler. Check that you're using (click)="toggleTheme()" on the IonButton element.

steps.hint:
Use an HTML

successCriteria:
The template contains a

element with interpolation showing 'Current theme: {{currentTheme}}'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a paragraph that displays the current theme value using Angular interpolation.
steps.feedbackPartial:
You're close! Make sure you added a paragraph element (

) with the exact text 'Current theme: {{currentTheme}}' using double curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element with theme interpolation is missing. Add a

tag with 'Current theme: {{currentTheme}}' inside the template.

steps.title: Apply theme classes dynamically
steps.instruction: Add an Angular class binding to the IonContent element that applies the 'dark-theme' CSS class when currentTheme equals 'dark'.
steps.hint: Use Angular's property binding syntax with square brackets: [class.class-name]="condition". The condition should check if currentTheme === 'dark'.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- In an Angular template -->
<ion-content [class.dark-theme]="currentTheme === 'dark'">
  <!-- Content here -->
</ion-content>
steps.expectedOutcome: The IonContent element will have the 'dark-theme' CSS class applied when currentTheme is 'dark', and removed when it's 'light'.
successCriteria: The IonContent element should have a class binding that conditionally applies 'dark-theme' based on the currentTheme value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added the dynamic class binding. Now the IonContent will have the 'dark-theme' class when the theme is dark, allowing you to style your app differently for dark mode.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the class binding might not be quite correct. Make sure you're using the exact syntax [class.dark-theme]="currentTheme === 'dark'" on the IonContent element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The class binding wasn't added correctly. You need to add [class.dark-theme]="currentTheme === 'dark'" to the IonContent element to dynamically apply the CSS class based on the theme.

steps.title: Add CSS for theme styling
steps.instruction: Add a styles array to the @Component decorator with CSS that defines styling for the '.dark-theme' class.
steps.hint: Inside the @Component decorator, add a styles property with an array containing CSS rules. Use the '.dark-theme' selector to style elements when dark mode is active.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have CSS styles defined for dark theme, which can be applied dynamically in the next step.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a 'styles' property with an array containing at least one CSS rule using the '.dark-theme' selector.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added CSS styles for the dark theme. The styles array is properly configured and ready to be applied when the theme changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the styles array might be missing or incomplete. Make sure you've added a 'styles' property to the @Component decorator with CSS rules using '.dark-theme' selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS styles for dark theme haven't been added correctly. Check that you've added a 'styles' array to the @Component decorator with proper CSS rules targeting '.dark-theme'.

steps.title: Test theme switching
steps.instruction: Click the toggle button in your app and verify that the theme text updates between 'light' and 'dark'.
steps.hint: Run your app, click the button, and watch the paragraph text change.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI shows 'Current theme: light' initially. When you click the button, it changes to 'Current theme: dark'. Clicking again reverts to 'light'.
successCriteria: The toggle button works and the displayed theme text updates correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! The theme toggle works perfectly. You've successfully implemented and tested dynamic theming in Ionic.
steps.feedbackPartial: The theme text updates, but make sure it toggles correctly between 'light' and 'dark' with each click.
steps.feedbackWrong: The theme text isn't updating. Check that the button's click handler is wired to toggleTheme() and that currentTheme is being updated.
